title: Federal implementation trails remain stage-bounded
summary: A qualitative map connecting thirteen Published implementation records across awards, obligations, delivered material, governance discontinuities, oversight limits, versioned software, local construction, procurement channels, and preliminary standards work.
map_question: What do current federal implementation records establish, and which later gates remain open before operating capability or scale?
interpretation_boundary: The map connects Published records that establish named financial actions, physical milestones, governance changes, oversight findings, research artifacts, facility construction, procurement channels, and preliminary specifications. Those stages remain distinct from completed facilities, accepted systems, operating infrastructure, institutional adoption, or scaled outcomes.

nodes.label: Stage-bounded implementation evidence
nodes.note: Published records now establish partial implementation trails and show that those trails can advance, split, stall, or reverse before operation and scale.

nodes.label: Awards, obligations, loans, and contracts
nodes.note: Talon, MP Materials, NAPMP, Southline, and OpenAI records identify instruments and amounts while separating value, obligation, outlay, construction, and delivery.

nodes.label: Produced and delivered project material
nodes.note: Project Pele's first TRISO fuel batch reached the demonstration site, upstream of reactor startup and operation.

nodes.label: Testbed and standards artifacts
nodes.note: NIST records laboratory infrastructure, testbed software, and accepted O-RAN contributions without claiming a completed wireless system.

nodes.label: Program governance discontinuity
nodes.note: Commerce's later NSTC and Natcast action requires the earlier advanced-packaging award stack to be revalidated recipient by recipient.

nodes.label: Prototype-to-production oversight gap
nodes.note: GAO documents a department-wide linkage limitation without making a finding about every individual prototype agreement.

nodes.label: Versioned research software
nodes.note: NIST's version 1.7 automation tool is a reproducible laboratory artifact upstream of certification and commercial adoption.

nodes.label: Local facility construction
nodes.note: Fab 3 topping out is a physical threshold upstream of occupancy, equipment qualification, production, and demonstrated local-system sufficiency.

nodes.label: Procurement and specification channels
nodes.note: Active purchasing channels and preliminary PIV drafts expose downstream implementation paths without proving adoption or completed migration.

links.note: Official award, obligation, loan, capacity-contract, and prototype-agreement records establish named financial actions.
Project Pele fuel production and delivery provide bounded physical evidence before reactor operation.
NIST's testbed, software, and incorporated contributions provide standards and test-infrastructure evidence.
A later program action can change the operator or agreement path and force earlier award claims to be revalidated.
Prototype awards need agreement-specific delivery and follow-on evidence because department-wide transition linkage is incomplete.
Version 1.7 supplies a documented release and laboratory configurations beneath the broader O-RAN project.
The Phoenix milestone shows a national semiconductor program entering a local construction system while utility, workforce, equipment, and operating gates remain open.
AI acquisition and credential modernization move through procurement, security, data, standards, validation, and adoption channels.

what_this_map_supports: Federal implementation can be analyzed as a sequence of distinct evidence stages rather than a single progress label.

Named Published records establish financial actions, delivered material, governance changes, oversight limits, software artifacts, construction milestones, procurement channels, and preliminary specifications.
A later governance action or oversight finding can change the interpretation of an earlier implementation record without proving that a specific project failed.
Local construction and operating conversion remain separate from national awards and program announcements.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not prove completed facilities, successful trials, production readiness, supplier security, grid delivery, accepted systems, institutional adoption, or scaled capability.
It does not establish that every NAPMP award was canceled, that any specific prototype failed, or that procurement and draft standards created operational adoption.
It does not rank technologies, programs, regions, or suppliers.
It does not create a numeric 42/59 score.
next_records_needed: Facility, equipment, commissioning, qualification, supplier, workforce, and production evidence behind Talon, MP Materials, and NAPMP.
Current Southline permits, financing, construction, interconnection, and energization records.
Project Pele startup and test evidence and OpenAI prototype delivery, evaluation, acceptance, and follow-on records.
Later wireless test, security, standards, certification, and deployment artifacts.
Recipient-level NSTC and NAPMP status, agency-specific AI procurement outcomes, formal PIV revisions, validated credential products, and completed migration milestones.
Phoenix facility permits, occupancy, utility service, equipment installation, qualification, production, and workforce outcomes.
